seoTitle: How to Enable TradingView on Tradovate for Direct Trading
metaDescription: See how to turn on the TradingView Add-On inside Tradovate, link your accounts, and place Market, Limit, and OCO orders straight from your TradingView chart.
intro: Trading from TradingView's charts while your orders execute through Tradovate's zero-commission futures desk sounds like it should be one toggle, but the permission for it lives in a settings menu most traders never open. This guide walks through turning on the TradingView Add-On inside Tradovate, granting TradingView access from the correct screen, and confirming the link actually works before you route real orders through it. It also covers the $9.99/month add-on cost and why testing with Paper Trading first is worth the extra five minutes.

steps.heading: Open Settings inside your Tradovate account
steps.body: Log into Tradovate and open Settings from the trading platform — you'll land on a tabbed menu covering Accounts, Subscriptions, Your Profile, Preferences, Security & Privacy, Transfers & Payments, Add-Ons, and API Access. The TradingView connection isn't under Preferences or API Access, which is where people usually look first; it's specifically under Add-Ons. Getting familiar with this menu matters beyond this one setup, since it's also where you manage your Tradovate subscription tier and any other platform integrations you add later.

image.caption: Tradovate's Settings panel, with Add-Ons listed alongside Accounts, Subscriptions, and API Access along the top.

steps.heading: Grant TradingView access from Add-Ons
steps.body: Inside the Add-Ons tab, find TradingView Integration and enable it — this is the step that actually authorizes TradingView to place orders through your Tradovate account. If you skip this and try to log into Tradovate directly from TradingView first, you'll hit an error explaining exactly what's missing: TradingView has not been entitled to access your account, and it points you back to the Client Dashboard's Add-Ons section to grant permission. That error is actually a useful confirmation you're in the right place — it means the two platforms are talking, just without permission granted yet.

steps.heading: Connect Tradovate from the TradingView side
steps.body: Back in TradingView, open the Trading Panel at the bottom of a chart and look for Tradovate among the broker connections listed there alongside names like TradeStation, CMC Markets, and Info Yatirim. Click through the Tradovate tile and log in with your Tradovate credentials when prompted. Once connected, TradingView's Trading Panel becomes a live extension of your Tradovate account — positions, watchlists, and your selected instrument all sync between the two.

image.caption: TradingView's Trading Panel, with Tradovate listed among the broker connections you can link an account to.

steps.heading: Place Market, Limit, and OCO orders from the chart
steps.body: With the accounts linked, you can trade the same instrument from either platform and see it reflected in both. Tradovate's own interface still shows the full order ticket, live DOM ladder, and position details — useful for double-checking exactly what TradingView just sent through. Market orders fill immediately at the current price, Limit orders wait for your specified level, and OCO (one-cancels-other) orders let you set a stop and a target simultaneously so one order cancels the other the moment either fills.

image.caption: Tradovate's own trading interface, showing the order ticket, DOM ladder, and live chart for an ES futures position.

steps.heading: Know what the add-on costs
steps.body: The TradingView Integration add-on runs about $9.99 a month on top of whatever Tradovate subscription tier you're already on. It's a small line item compared to commissions on most other futures platforms, but it's worth checking your Tradovate billing under Subscriptions so it doesn't come as a surprise on your next statement.

steps.heading: Test the connection with Paper Trading first
steps.body: Before routing real money through the integration, switch to Paper Trading in Tradovate and run through a handful of Market, Limit, and OCO orders from TradingView to confirm they land correctly. This catches the two most common issues early — a permission that didn't fully save, or an order type that doesn't behave the way you expected — without any financial downside. Once a few paper trades fill and cancel exactly as intended, you can switch back to your live account with confidence the routing works.

faq.question: Does the TradingView Add-On cost extra on Tradovate?
faq.answer: Yes, the TradingView Integration add-on is priced separately at around $9.99 per month in addition to your regular Tradovate subscription.

faq.question: Can I place Market, Limit, and OCO orders from TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, once the add-on is enabled and your accounts are linked, you can submit Market, Limit, and OCO orders directly from the TradingView chart.

faq.question: Why does TradingView say it's not entitled to access my account?
faq.answer: That error means the connection reached Tradovate but permission hasn't been granted yet. Log into the Tradovate Client Dashboard, open Add-Ons, and enable TradingView Integration there.

faq.question: Is it safe to link my TradingView account to Tradovate?
faq.answer: The integration is designed to securely connect the two accounts so order instructions pass through without exposing your login credentials to the other platform.

faq.question: Should I test the integration before trading live?
faq.answer: Yes, using Paper Trading first lets you confirm orders route correctly before you commit real funds.
